earlier_scan.note: Extinct; attested only by a Koelle 1854 wordlist — no phonological description exists.

sources.citation: Koelle, Sigismund Wilhelm. 1854. Polyglotta Africana; or, A comparative vocabulary of nearly three hundred words and phrases in more than one hundred distinct African languages. London: Church Missionary House. Preface p. vi; Introductory Remarks p. 20 (no. XII.B.21 'Afudu or Afaru'); Afudu column no. 21 in the vocabulary tables.
sources.note: No language-specific statement. Preface p. vi lists the notation for the whole book: '´ the common sign for the accent, e.g., á, ó.' The Afudu column carries acute marks on many items (e.g. printed p. 3: one 'do & kádo', two 'mbéfe & béfai', three 'mbétori & bétori'), but nothing says what the accent is or where it falls. The p. 20 notice is an informant biography (Abitso/John Second of Bititi near Betson, capital burnt by 'Beliyi or Bedeyi'; countrymen in Sierra Leone 'some of whom have quite forgotten their language').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record afud1235 'Afudu' (Hammarström et al.), with reference list: Koelle 1854; Latham 1862; Johnston 1919-22; Meek 1922; Williamson 1971 (all typed overview/wordlist; no descriptive source).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; editorial comment: 'Afudu is a language only known from a wordlist in Koelle 1854... presumably extinct... location identified as southeast of Takum in Nigeria by Meek (Semi-Bantu:223)... placed in Bantoid by Williamson (Benue-Congo:277).'

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1922. A comparative study of the Bantu and semi-Bantu languages, vol. 2. Oxford: Clarendon Press. 'Group U (S-B.): the Southern Benue languages (No. 249)', p. 176; also p. 220ff. prefix summary.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Discusses only noun-class prefixes ('Classes 1, 2, 5, 7, 8a, 9, 11, and 13 are certainly represented'), numerals ('counting in Afudu seems to be by tens') and the negative suffix -ke, all 'from our very scanty information' (Koelle).

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A comparative study of the Bantu and semi-Bantu languages, vol. 1. Oxford: Clarendon Press. Afudu = language no. 249 (location note in the language list; Koelle's items reproduced in the comparative vocabulary columns).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent for Afudu; only '249. Afudu is — or was — the language of a small country south of the Benue river, east of the Munshi region, and south of the Juku country.'

sources.citation: Latham, Robert Gordon. 1862. Elements of comparative philology. London: Walton & Maberly. (Index entry 'Afudu vocabulary'; Koelle's Benue items reprinted in the 'Languages of the Gabun, etc.' tables, p. 565 area.)
sources.note: Nothing; a reprint of Koelle vocabulary items without diacritics or comment.
